A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CoDiLA research. Their text, figures, tables, equations, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material relocated between versions.

before.justification: V1 reports original training-loss measurements, code-generation accuracy and throughput, and conditioning and candidate-scope ablations in Section 4 and Appendix A.

after.justification: V2 retains these empirical results and adds original infilling, waiting-line planning, graph-traversal, and ablation results in Section 4 and Appendices B–C.

M1.justification: V2 adds an AR verification mode that penalizes disagreement with DLM predictions, plus global decoding with EOS penalties (Section 3.5). Appendix C introduces mixed-entropy infilling with fallback rules and graph-traversal verification through remasking. These substantially extend inference procedures; the original soft-conditioning architecture and training objective remain.

E1.justification: V1 evaluates code generation on HumanEval, MBPP, their enhanced test suites, and BigCodeBench. V2 retains these and adds HumanEval-Infilling, ParallelBench waiting-line tasks, and graph-traversal planning, including task-specific training. Missing-span generation with surrounding context and synthetic planning substantially broaden task coverage.

E2.justification: The original Dream-Coder and ADJUST comparisons remain. V2 adds standalone Qwen3-0.6B results and comparisons against DreamOn, Dream-Instruct-7B, and MGDM in the added tasks. Table 2 also includes Deepseek-Coder-6.7B, Seed-Coder-8B, and Qwen2.5-Coder-7B reference scores, explicitly attributed to Wu et al. rather than newly run experiments.

E3.justification: Section 4.2 changes controlled masking from 8-token to 32-token segments and extends tested block sizes to 16 and 32, making the training-loss plots different-setting results. New experiments vary AR size, batch size, and blocks decoded per iteration, introduce a code-extraction-failure metric, and specify additional task-specific training and decoding protocols. The original code-generation configurations in Table 3 remain.

E4.justification: V2 retains the Top-1 conditioning and local-horizon analyses while adding Top-3/Top-5 conditioning, boundary-token removal, AR-size controls, global EOS penalization, one-versus-two-block decoding, generation-order correlations, batching, and code-extraction error analysis. These investigate substantial additional questions about mechanism, decoding flexibility, and efficiency.

E5.justification: Both versions specify a single-sample, fixed-seed evaluation in Appendix A.2. Neither introduces repeated-run uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The new Spearman correlations analyze generation order rather than uncertainty in reported performance.

E6.justification: Figures 4–5 and the original conditioning and scope results are retained. Numerous new results appear: v2 Table 2 reports 62.5% infilling accuracy at 1.3 tokens/step versus DreamOn's 62.5% at one token/step; Table 9 reports 63.1% versus 52.6% waiting-line accuracy at K=8. Graph-traversal and additional ablation results also appear. Table 6's one-block HumanEval values conflict with Table 4, preventing a reliable interpretation of those entries as same-setting updates.

T1.justification: Theorems 3.2–3.3 and their proofs remain unchanged after relocation from Appendix B to D. Section 3.5 makes a limited mathematical correction: the partial-block entropy domain changes from k≤L/B to k≤B, and full-block entropy is evaluated at B instead of L/B.

C1.justification: Both versions claim improved block-factorized modeling, a compact soft-conditioned AR component, better code-generation accuracy–latency tradeoffs, approximately twofold dynamic-decoding speedup, and preserved bidirectional capabilities. V2 explicitly names infilling and planning in the contribution list, but the added evidence principally substantiates the existing capability claim.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations that improvements do not depend on strong standalone AR coding ability, global EOS penalties overcome the need for local scoping, generation becomes less left-to-right, and batching amortizes AR overhead. Some interpretations overreach: Appendix B.1 calls full soft-conditioning strictly Pareto-optimal, although Table 4 gives Top-5 higher HumanEval accuracy at B=4, 56.1% versus 51.8%, at the same reported throughput.

D1.justification: Most original Appendix A implementation details remain. V2 adds a code-access statement and extensive instructions for new configurations, including infilling entropy weight 0.5 and fallbacks, waiting-line disagreement penalty 1.0, and graph-model architecture and training epochs. These materially expand reproducibility information; the PDF establishes the repository disclosure, not its external availability.

R1.justification: V2 adds references for InCoder, the evaluation harness, DreamOn, diffusion-based planning, and Swordsman. The related-work positioning otherwise remains substantially unchanged. DiffuCoder's change from a 2025 preprint citation to a 2026 conference citation represents the same work, not an added research comparison.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized rewrites to generation strategies and experimental narration, reorganizes ablations into Appendix B, and moves proofs to Appendix D. Most introduction, theoretical, and related-work prose remains. Author contribution markings and publication information also change; much of the additional text documents new scientific content rather than extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: Figure 3 is redrawn for five block sizes, and Figures 6–7 add multipanel AR-size and decoding-scope comparisons. New tables display errors, infilling, planning, ordering, batching, and multiple-block results. V1 Table 1 becomes the expanded v2 Table 4; the original scope table becomes Table 5, and Figure 5 moves unchanged. These substantially expand the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: V1 largely supports preserved non-causal capabilities through architectural arguments; v2 directly tests infilling and planning and adds controls examining AR capacity, global decoding, and computational overhead. This closes an important empirical gap and substantially improves understanding and reproducibility. The gains outweigh localized reporting weaknesses, particularly the Table 4 Pareto overclaim and Table 6 inconsistencies. Unchanged uncertainty reporting still limits confidence in small measured differences.
